key_insight: MoREGT combines schema-routed relational experts with label-blind, agent-derived features to improve cross-database prediction using far less pretraining data than a large-corpus baseline.
engineering_relevance: Schema-aware modeling and validated feature generation offer a practical route to transferring predictive models across platforms with different relational databases.
method: Represent rows and cells as graph-transformer tokens, adding row log-ages and foreign-key relationship names to attention.
Route row and cell tokens to experts using column metadata rather than values.
Use a label-blind LLM agent to create validated single-row derived columns from target schema and column statistics.
evidence_signal: Across 21 RelBench tasks with leave-one-database-out pretraining on six databases, agent features raised mean AUROC from 78.45 to 79.63 and lowered mean nMAE from 27.91 to 26.98, outperforming compared methods including RT-J, pretrained on roughly 400× as many databases.
watch_item: Results are limited to the reported RelBench evaluation; deployment requires validating generated features and preventing label or temporal leakage.
paper_title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization
